title: Soft GPU partitioning + preemptive KV tiering for predictable weights/KV/activation budgets
creator: Jamal Ortiz
description:
Problem: Peak memory contention between model weights, KV cache, and activation working sets causes unpredictable tail latency and reactive evictions. Current hard partition approaches are either overprovisioned (wasteful) or brittle under bursty tenant traffic.

Proposal: Implement a 'soft partitioning' memory advisor and runtime enforcement policy that treats weights, KV, and activations as elastic bands rather than fixed slices. Components: 1) a lightweight Memory Ledger service that projects short-horizon (0-60s) consumption per class using recent token arrival patterns and model sequence distributions; 2) Preemptive KV Tiering with two soft-preemption bands (grace / immediate) that allow KV to be downgraded to compressed/quantized slots or staged for eviction before activations are affected; 3) Activation spill hints to trigger cooperative batching reductions or transient slower-start policies for long-context requests; 4) A simulation harness to validate SLO trade-offs against representative tenant mixes.

Why this is different: instead of fixed reserve accounting, the advisor continuously rebalances an allocation budget and exposes a simple API for the scheduler and batcher to request temporary extra headroom or accept preemption. This reduces tail evictions and lowers average reserved headroom while keeping latency SLOs intact.
acceptance_criteria: Memory Ledger service running in staging projecting per-class budgets with <= 10% forecast error at 30s horizon for our topology traces
KV preemption policy implemented with two tiers and validated in simulator showing >= 35% fewer activation evictions under mixed workloads compared to static partitioning
APIs exposed for scheduler/batcher: /request_headroom and /notify_preempt with clear response codes and backoff guidance
End-to-end experiment demonstrating no more than 5% P99 latency regression for critical customers while reducing reserved headroom by >= 15% versus current baseline
Documentation and runbook added: design doc, operational dashboard, rollout checklist and rollback conditions
tasks: Design data schema and projection algorithm for Memory Ledger (time series windowing, decay, expectation)
Implement Ledger prototype (Rust service) with a gRPC shim for the runtime to poll budgets
Add KV tiering codepath: compressed slot allocator + staged eviction queue
Wire scheduler/batcher to call /request_headroom and honor preemption hints
Build simulator scenarios (tenant mixes, spike traces) and compare against static partition baseline
Create dashboard panels: forecast vs actual, preemption events, eviction counts, headroom utilization
Run staged canary on one Dedicated pool with synthetic spike traffic and measure SLOs
Author runbook for on-call: key metrics to watch, thresholds for auto-rollback
notes: Projection model: use exponential moving average on token arrival + weighted sequence length histogram per-route; keep model simple for low CPU overhead
Favor preemption of cold KV slots (long-unused prefixes) before evicting recent activations
Compression for KV tier: 4-bit quantized keys for first-tier downgrade; CPU decompression cost acceptable compared to activation re-compute
Policy knobs: grace_window (ms), immediate_threshold (bytes), emergency_cut_ratio; expose via cluster config for tuning
We need to reconcile with current reservation ledger used by Dedicated capacity billing to avoid billing regressions
